newsitem.title: UK: Trans-Zambezi Industries pretax profit up 42 pct.
newsitem.headline: Trans-Zambezi Industries pretax profit up 42 pct.

text.p: Southern African conglomerate Trans-Zambezi Industries Limited, which intends to seek a partial listing in London in January, reported pretax profit up over 42 percent from 1995 in preliminary results on Thursday.
A statement from TZI Ltd, already listed in Luxembourg, said profit before tax for the year ended September 30 was around $15.8 million from $11.6 million in 1995.
Profit attributable to shareholders increased 30 percent on the year, headline earnings per share were up 23.5 percent to 32.6 cents and attributable net assets per share grew by 27 percent.
CEO Hilary Duckworth said the business faced strong organic growth, with "a healthy outlook for demand in the region and the likelihood of further complementary investment opportunities".

TZI said its market capitalisation rose to $111 million from $40 million after the most recent capital-raising in August, when 16.75 million shares were issued at $2.25/share. There are some 46 million shares in issues with institutional holders including Morgan Stanley, Mercury Asset Management and Robeco.
The company is also seeking a listing on the stock exchanges of Zimbabwe and Zambia, where its holdings are concentrated.

Of the three main divisions, the contribution from Financial Services and Industrial were both up threefold on the year, while Food and Distribution returned a 72 percent increase in attributable profits.

TZI said its Madison Insurance company in Zambia had had a difficult year "reflecting the lack of liquidity in the Zambian economy" and the performance of the small Botswana associate in the Food and Distribution division was "disappointing".
The company's battery producer Chloride "benefited from the temporary window' caused by industrial action in South Africa which stemmed the inflow of imported product".

"While tariff reforms are expected to be announced shortly in Zimbabwe, the year has been disappointing in terms of achieving a measure of protection against dumping' of products from South Africa," a report with the results said.

Duckworth said the group ended the year with large cash resources and poised to "benefit from rising prosperity in the region". The third dividend of 3.5 cents/share will be paid on March 10 to shareholders registered on January 2, 1997.
